title: Rubble accumulation around a fixed cylinder: geometry growth law, shielding factor, steady-state scaling
decision: Does a 3-D soft-sphere DEM of a driven broken-ice field reproduce (a) an exponential saturation of the accumulation geometry, (b) a Froude-number controlled shielding-to-amplification transition of the front pressure, and (c) a mass-conserving open-system balance? Decision = accept / honest-FAIL per observable, never a single global pass.
alternatives: A. 3-D soft-sphere DEM with a force-limited servo platen, blocks = 2-D-periodic flume cross-section (chosen: only route that keeps grain-scale contact mechanics while bounding cost)
B. Continuum shallow-granular (depth-averaged) pile model: cheap but not DEM, no contact statistics, rejected as it cannot be checked against contact-level conservation
C. 2-D vertical-plane wedge model: cannot express the plan-view width B_p, which is one of the three required geometry observables
hypothesis: H1: L_p(t), B_p(t), H_p(t) follow y = y_inf (1 - exp(-t/tau)) with R^2 > 0.95 once the pile is in the flux-limited growth regime

H2: R_shield = p_front / p_0 < 1 at low Fr (accumulation spreads the load) and >= 1 at high Fr (the pile cannot consolidate and the resident blocks load the structure dynamically), with a crossover Fr
H3: the steady geometry scales as a power law in Fr and C_i
H4: mass closes to < 2 % between the kinematic inventory and the outflow bookkeeping

metrics.geometry: L_p = (-R) - x_2%, B_p = 2|y|_98%, H_p = z_98% + r - z_ref  (percentiles over the resident pile set)
metrics.load: p_front = mean(Fx on the upstream half of the cylinder)/(D h_i), time-averaged over the last 25 % of the run
metrics.baseline: p_0 from the *sweeper* twin: identical field, geometry and driving, blocks inside R + 2.5 r removed every step
metrics.steady_geometry: exponential plateau y_inf, cross-checked with the time average over the last 25 %

predeclared_thresholds.growth_fit_pass: R^2 > 0.95 on the fitted window, reported raw and with a fixed 11-sample centred moving average
predeclared_thresholds.fit_window_rule: starts when the measured quantity first exceeds 2 % of its run maximum (the feed transit is not part of the growth law)
predeclared_thresholds.mass_closure_pass: partition error < 0.02 relative; capture-zone crossing-vs-inventory error < 0.05 (Euler integration of the crossings)
predeclared_thresholds.convergence: y(t_end)/y_inf >= 0.95 for L, B and H; otherwise the case is flagged and excluded from the steady-state scaling fits
predeclared_thresholds.resolution: h_i/(2r) >= 0.75 (at least three-quarter of a block diameter across the ice sheet); below that the case is flagged unresolved and excluded from the scaling fits
predeclared_thresholds.negative_controls: C_i = 0 -> zero blocks and zero pile; v_i = 0 -> pile mass and H_p exactly zero (no growth)
predeclared_thresholds.component_of_change: exponents from log-log least squares with the standard error reported; a literature comparison is only claimed where a single authoritative value exists, otherwise range containment is reported and the exponent claim is WITHHELD

controlled: block diameter 2r = h_i / layer_target (capped by the particle budget)
domain in units of D (upstream 2D, downstream 1D, half width 1.25D)
confounders: number of block layers across the sheet (varies with D/h_i given the count budget)
domain confinement (half width 1.25 D) which limits lateral bypass
driving pressure (sets the absolute load level; a sensitivity case at 2x particle budget is included)
surface tension/freeze bonding absent, so the pile cannot be cohesive
variables_and_confounders.repetitions: one seed for the full grid (126 cases); determinism verified by a same-seed duplicate in the unit tests; a doubled and a halved particle budget at (D=3, h=0.25, C=0.5, v=0.3) probes the resolution sensitivity

stopping_rule: each case runs to t_end = 3 tau_flux + 0.5 transit, tau_flux = 0.8 D/(C_i v_i), capped at 150 s of physical time and 26 000 timesteps; the sweep stops when all cases are done. No case is extended because of its result.

analysis.aggregation: plateau values from the per-case fit; steady-window means as a cross-check
analysis.power_law_fit: ordinary least squares in log-log space, exponent with standard error and R^2
analysis.outliers: none removed; cases that fail the convergence, resolution or plateau checks are flagged and excluded from the scaling fit only
analysis.uncertainty: standard error of the exponent; no bootstrap (single seed per case)

interpretation_limits: blocks are spheres: no interlocking, no freeze bonds, no crushing; the emergent internal friction is a model property
the flume idealisation (free-slip lateral walls at 1.25 D) suppresses lateral bypass, so the accumulation is stronger than at an isolated cylinder in an unbounded field
the number of block layers across the sheet is 1-3, so the sail height is resolved to about one block diameter
p_front is a time-averaged momentum flux on the upstream half, not a local pressure distribution
